subject: DPA addendum: sovereignty clauses, transient failover windows & subprocessor timeline
messages:
From: Luke Bryant <legal@acmehealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: ACME Security Team <security@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Data sovereignty commitments + subprocessor timeline

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the deep dive yesterday. Per our procurement checklist and the regulator brief we have two items we need Redwood to commit to before we advance to our exec approval: 

1) Data residency commitment: we need a DPA addendum that (a) states production content for Acme Health customers originating in the EU will be stored and processed in EU-only infrastructure, and (b) allows for a transient failover to non-EU regions only for disaster/failover events with an explicit maximum window (we're proposing 72 hours) and required notification/recording in audit logs.

2) Subprocessor and KMS detail: a full roster of subprocessors with planned onboarding timeline (not just current but those we may add in the next 6 months). We also need to confirm whether customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) can be used and whether KMS key material will ever leave the EU.

Attached is a short tech appendix from our architects that shows the expected call pattern and where temporary KV syncs would occur (ACME_Technical_Reqs.pdf). Can you confirm whether Redwood can:
- Provide the DPA addendum language for our counsel to review,
- Provide the subprocessor roster and intended onboarding dates, and
- Confirm the KMS residency guarantees (or provide the exact failure-mode where key material might transit regions).

We prefer a written addendum we can route through Legal, and ideally a short call tomorrow to close open points.

Best,
Luke Bryant
Legal Counsel, Acme Health

----
Attachment: ACME_Technical_Reqs.pdf (pdf)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Luke Bryant <legal@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data sovereignty commitments + subprocessor timeline

Luke —

Thanks for the clear list and the appendix. We can absolutely get you a redline and the roster. High-level answers up front so your counsel has context while we prepare the document: 

- DPA addendum: Redwood can offer a strengthened addendum that includes a contractual commitment to resident processing for EU-origin data under normal operations, and an explicit transient-failover clause limited to emergency/disaster scenarios. Our standard transient window proposal is 48 hours, but we can support 72 hours with additional monitoring and notification steps (we'd like to capture those in the addendum).

- Subprocessors: we'll provide the current roster plus a 6-month onboarding roadmap. We provide 30 days' advance notice for any new subprocessor that would have access to production data; the roster export will include expected onboarding month and category (infra, logging, analytics).

- KMS: BYOK is available for Dedicated and Private customers. For Hosted accounts we offer customer-managed keys in specific regions; we will confirm whether the key material is ever exported during emergency replication. Short answer: key material is not exported; replication uses encrypted key-wrapped transfer and customer keys remain under the region-specific KMS when BYOK is used. We'll provide the precise technical appendix to include as exhibit.

I've attached a first-pass redline to the DPA addendum (Redwood_DPA_Addendum_v1.docx). Marissa — looping you and Hannah for legal + privacy language and to capture any billing/SLA implications for a 72-hour failover commitment. Markus — can you confirm the operational detection/notification timeline we'd include (automated alert + manual confirmation windows)?

If that sounds right, let's schedule a 30-min call tomorrow 10:00-10:30 PT to walk counsel through the redline and the roster.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Sr. Manager, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

----
Attachment: Redwood_DPA_Addendum_v1.docx (docx)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Luke Bryant <legal@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data sovereignty commitments + subprocessor timeline

Luke / Rachel —

Thanks for the doc, Rachel. A few notes from Legal/Privacy Ops after a quick read of v1: 

- Failover window: we can accept 72 hours as a ceiling, provided we include (1) obligation to notify Acme within 2 hours of failover start, (2) post-incident report within 7 business days, and (3) an option for expedited remediation if Acme requests it (may have cost implications).

- Scope language: the addendum should be explicit about "EU-origin production content" and exclude aggregated telemetry used solely for platform reliability (we'll include an explicit carve-out for telemetry and metrics with examples).

- Subprocessor timeline & audit rights: we can provide a 6-month roadmap and 30-day notice for changes. For customers with elevated regulatory needs (like Acme), we can offer an annual on-site/virtual audit or SOC excerpt under NDA; that should be captured as an optional clause.

- KMS phrase: suggest replacing "key material is not exported" with the slightly more defined line "customer key material will not be exported from the region's KMS; key-wrapped replication keys may be used for failover but will not grant Redwood plaintext access." That helps our security team's acceptance criteria.

Markus — what telemetry/alerting cadence can we commit to? Rachel, once we finalize wording, we'll need to confirm if this triggers any change in pricing for Hosted customers who want the 72-hour contractual limit (we may need to upsell a 'geo-bounded SLA' add-on).

I'll incorporate these points into v2 and attach the updated doc + a CSV export of the current subprocessor roster for Acme's review.

Marissa Cole
Head of Legal Operations, Redwood Inference

----
Attachment: subprocessors_roster.csv (csv)

From: Luke Bryant <legal@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, ACME Security Team <security@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 10:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data sovereignty commitments + subprocessor timeline

Marissa / Rachel —

Appreciate the fast turnaround and the clarifications. The proposed notification cadence and the KMS wording tweak look reasonable to us. We'll review the roster and the updated v2 addendum when you send it. Two quick asks before tomorrow's call: 

1) Can you include an exhibit (technical appendix) that briefly explains how key-wrapped replication works in failover so our security team can verify there is no possibility of plaintext key export?

2) Please send a DocuSign-ready copy of the v2 addendum once final so our counsel can route it to Execs.

We're available for the 10:00-10:30 PT slot and will have one of our security architects on the line.

Thanks,
Luke Bryant
Legal Counsel, Acme Health
